claims.claim: Dealer in all kinds of Japanese parts and gearbox
claims.evidence: The witness report only shows a used drivetrain/engine-gearbox assembly; it does not confirm the seller’s business type or inventory.

risks.risk: Exact compatibility is unknown (vehicle make/model, engine code, gearbox/transfer-case type, mounting/shaft splines). Wrong fit can make the unit unusable.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the identification plate/engine code/gearbox code and the mounting/bracket side showing part numbers (or a video test-fit showing alignment with the buyer’s vehicle).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as a generic used drivetrain unit with unknown compatibility; buyer should assume possible mismatch and budget for returns/extra parts.

risks.risk: Completeness is unknown (starter, alternator, turbo, ECU, sensors, wiring harness length, mounts, linkage). Missing components reduce value.
risks.proof: A full laid-out inventory photo/video showing every included component and what is not included (including ECU/sensors/hoses/mounts/actuators).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as incomplete/unknown completeness; treat missing electronics/sensors/mounts as not guaranteed.

risks.risk: Operational condition is unknown (whether it was running before removal; gearbox shift quality; clutch condition if applicable).
risks.proof: Video clip of the unit running/engaging gears before removal (or a bench test video showing gear engagement and no abnormal noises).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as not proven working; assume overhaul/repair may be needed.

risks.risk: Leak status is unknown (oil/coolant/gear oil leaks and source).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all seals/gaskets and a short clip showing the unit after cleaning (or a drip/leak check).
risks.if_unproven: Priced as potentially leaking/needs resealing; assume buyer will replace gaskets/seals.

risks.risk: Internal wear/defects are unknown (bearings, gears, timing components, transfer-case internals). Dusty exterior does not confirm internal health.
risks.proof: Any service/repair record plus a teardown photo of internal components OR a functional test with load (gear engagement under load) showing smooth operation.
risks.if_unproven: Priced at worst-case used condition (possible internal wear) rather than “good working”.

risks.risk: Potential scam/overstatement risk: seller may claim it’s a Japanese gearbox/parts dealer, but the specific unit’s identity and condition are not verifiable from the photos.
risks.proof: Clear part numbers/serials and proof of origin (invoice/receipt) matching the unit shown.
risks.if_unproven: Priced conservatively as a high-uncertainty used drivetrain unit until identity and working condition are proven.

proof_requests: Send clear photos of the engine/gearbox code/serial plate (and any stamped numbers) and the exact gearbox type/transfer-case markings.
Show a complete parts list: what is included vs missing (starter, alternator, turbo, ECU, sensors, mounts, linkage, wiring harness, hoses).
Provide a video of the unit running and engaging gears (or a bench test) before removal, including any shift/engagement sound checks.
Provide leak proof: photos of seals/gaskets and a short clip after cleaning showing no fresh leaks.
Provide compatibility info: mounting/bracket photos and shaft/spline details so it matches the buyer’s vehicle.
response.reason: The witness can identify the item type as a used drivetrain/engine-gearbox assembly, so it can be priced at its worst-case as an unverified, potentially incomplete, compatibility-unknown unit. Seller’s words about being a Japanese parts/gearbox dealer are not verifiable from the report.
